## Overview

ResearchOS capabilities are modular methods that expose specialist Android functionality to an XLSForm workflow.

A capability should have:

- a canonical ID;
- declared inputs and outputs;
- structured status and errors;
- provenance metadata;
- a dashboard tester;
- a complete XLSForm example;
- offline and compatibility documentation.

## Capability families

### Sense

Acquire observations from onboard or connected sensors.

Examples include:

- environmental sensors;
- Bluetooth Low Energy devices;
- ESP32-based instruments;
- phone sensors.

### Identify

Identify people, objects, devices or records.

Examples include:

- QR codes;
- barcodes;
- NFC tags;
- RFID readers;
- device registration.

### Measure

Produce quantitative measurements or derived values.

Examples include:

- spatial geometry;
- sensor measurements;
- computer-vision measurements;
- instrument readings.

### Verify

Provide evidence about identity, integrity or execution.

Examples include:

- device attestation;
- biometric or device-authenticated confirmation;
- digital signatures;
- OpenPGP verification.

### Communicate

Exchange messages or trigger communication workflows.

Examples include:

- SMS;
- email integration;
- notifications;
- peer-to-peer transfer.

### Invoke

Call another Android application, service or provider.

Examples include:

- navigation applications;
- external scanners;
- approved third-party application interfaces;
- provider command adapters.

### Compute

Run a local analytical or machine-learning method.

Examples include:

- image classification;
- translation;
- speech transcription;
- approved Termux-backed methods.

### Navigate

Open or monitor a navigation workflow.

Examples include:

- navigate to coordinates;
- navigate along a GPX route;
- add map markers;
- inspect route progress.

### Output

Send information to an external device or presentation layer.

Examples include:

- label printing;
- device displays;
- local file export.

### Schedule

Launch an EDC workflow at a defined time or recurrence.

The scheduler starts the form. The form can then invoke ResearchOS capabilities as part of the normal workflow.

## Current modules

The exact set of modules depends on the ResearchOS build.

The current project includes or is developing modules for:

- NFC;
- QR codes and barcodes;
- SMS;
- random number generation;
- native question primitives;
- sensors and connected devices;
- document scanning;
- speech transcription;
- on-device translation;
- computer vision;
- provider commands;
- attestation;
- scheduling.

## Native protocols and outputs

ResearchOS can now run simple native protocols without handing every step to an external form app. A configured capability can be saved as a preset, presets can be chained into a named protocol, and the whole run can be exported as one output package.

Each exported package has a stable `researchos_submission_id`. The same UUID appears in the output folder/filename and inside the JSON, and protocol steps share the same UUID. This makes the exported JSON suitable as a submission-level record for later parsing in R.

## Capability documentation

Each capability page should state:

- purpose;
- capability ID;
- setup requirements;
- provider requirements;
- permissions;
- inputs;
- outputs;
- status and errors;
- offline behaviour;
- example XLSForm;
- limitations;
- tested versions.

## Provider adapters

A canonical capability may be supplied by more than one provider.

For example:

``` text
scanner.capture
    ├── researchos_internal
    ├── zxing_compatible
    ├── datawedge
    └── proglove
```

The canonical interface should remain stable even when the provider changes.

## Choosing a capability

Choose a capability based on the operation the workflow needs, not the application that happens to implement it.

Prefer:

``` text
navigate.to
```

over a direct dependency on a particular Android activity.
